items.description: The deliverable shapes this bounty accepts. Every bounty accepts any combination of `content_url` (posted links) and `media` (uploaded files), except `data_capture` bounties, whose proof is clips recorded in the Whop app that accumulate on the attempt.

accepted_submissions_limit.description: Number of submissions that can be accepted (winner slots).

accepted_submissions_per_user_limit.description: How many winner slots one worker can win. Defaults to `1`. Wins plus proofs awaiting review never exceed this number, and a worker runs one attempt at a time. Cannot exceed `accepted_submissions_limit`.

items.description: Proof livestreams live on this bounty right now, newest first — workers streaming their attempts. Empty when nothing is live.

affiliate_share_amount.description: What a referrer earns per accepted submission when the worker arrived through their affiliate link, in whole currency units, at the standard platform fee rate. Taken out of the worker's post-fee reward rather than added on top. `0` when the bounty pays no affiliate share, including bounties tied to no account, which cannot record a referral.

items.description: Countries whose residents can work the bounty, as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes. Empty means worldwide.

awaiting_review_submissions_count.description: Submissions delivered and waiting on review. A subset of `unresolved_submissions_count`, which also counts attempts still in progress.

budget_amount.description: Total gross budget committed to the bounty: `gross_reward_amount` times `accepted_submissions_limit`.

business_goal_type.description: What the poster wants the work to achieve, declared once at create. `null` for bounties created before the taxonomy rolled out.

cancel_requested_at.description: When cancellation was requested, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. On a `closed` bounty this means the cancel is pending: submissions are stopped and the bounty cancels once in-flight submissions resolve. On a `canceled` bounty it records when the cancellation was requested. `null` when no cancellation was ever requested.

capture_spec.description: The technical contract footage must be recorded against. Present only on `data_capture` bounties; `null` for every other goal type.

created_at.description: When the bounty was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Currency for all amounts on the bounty, as a lowercase ISO 4217 code.

description.description: Full task instructions shown to workers.
description.example: Record one continuous pass of a full interior detail, dash to trunk, on a customer vehicle.

discussion_experience_id.description: Experience the bounty's discussion thread lives in, prefixed `exp_`. Read this — not `experience_id` — to open the thread: a platform-wide bounty has no hosting experience of its own but its discussion still lives in one.

discussion_feed_id.description: Forum feed containing the bounty's discussion thread. `null` for a bounty with no forum post.

discussion_post_id.description: Forum post anchoring the bounty's discussion thread. Read together with `discussion_experience_id` to address the thread. `null` for a bounty with no forum post.

experience_id.description: Experience the bounty is hosted in, prefixed `exp_`. `null` for platform-wide bounties; may belong to a different account than the funder.

funding_account.description: Account whose balance funds the bounty pool, or `null` when a user funds it personally. May differ from the account hosting `experience_id`.

gross_paid_out_amount.description: Gross amount paid out from the bounty pool across accepted submissions — worker payouts, platform fees, and affiliate shares together. Tips and reviewer rewards are excluded.

gross_reward_amount.description: Gross bounty-pool amount allocated per accepted submission, in whole currency units.

hosting_account.description: Account hosting the bounty's forum — the one whose `route` and `experience_id` address its discussion thread, and where its submissions dashboard lives. `null` for a platform-wide bounty with no host. May differ from `funding_account`.

id.description: Bounty ID, prefixed `bnty_`.

min_total_verified_duration_seconds.description: Total verified footage a submission must accumulate before it can be submitted, in seconds. Always a whole number of hours. Present only on `data_capture` bounties — it is what `net_reward_amount` pays for, so rate displays divide by it. `null` for every other goal type.

net_reward_amount.description: What a worker is quoted per accepted submission after the platform fee, in whole currency units. The exact post-fee figure, at the standard platform fee rate — a worker who locked a different rate, or who arrived through an affiliate link, is paid a different amount.

poster.description: User who posted the bounty — the account owner when created with an account API key.

scheduled_frequency.description: How often the schedule creates a new bounty. Each occurrence is a separate bounty; the original is not republished.

scheduled_publish_at.description: When a scheduled bounty will publish, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` once published, for bounties that were never scheduled, and for terminally failed drafts parked for manual rescheduling.

spots_remaining.description: Unfilled winner capacity: `accepted_submissions_limit` minus `accepted_submissions_count`, clamped to zero. Not on its own a signal that the bounty accepts new claims — read `status` for that: only an `open` bounty takes new submissions.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `scheduled` bounties are unpublished drafts, visible to their poster and the account's authorized managers; `open` bounties accept new submissions; `closed` bounties are live but no longer accept new submissions; `completed` bounties paid out every winner slot; `canceled` bounties ended before filling their slots.

submissions_closed_at.description: When new submissions stopped being accepted, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Set when a cancellation is requested on a bounty with work in flight, so in-flight submissions can resolve before the bounty cancels. `null` when submissions were never stopped — including completed bounties that simply filled every winner slot.

title.description: Short name of the task shown to workers.

unresolved_submissions_count.description: Submissions still awaiting an outcome: in progress or pending review.

updated_at.description: When the bounty was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

viewer_accepted_submissions_count.description: How many winner slots the authenticated user has already won on this bounty. Read against `accepted_submissions_per_user_limit` to show a worker their remaining allowance. `0` when the request has no authenticated user.

host.description: User hosting the proof livestream — the worker streaming their attempt. `null` if the host account no longer exists.

id.description: Livestream feed ID.

title.description: Display title for the proof livestream.

bounty_submission_id.description: The bounty submission (attempt) this clip belongs to, prefixed `btys_`.

created_at.description: When the clip was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

duration_seconds.description: Server-validated clip duration in whole seconds. `null` until validation completes.

failure_code.description: Stable validation failure code. `null` unless `status` is `failed`.

failure_message.description: Human-readable validation failure reason. `null` unless `status` is `failed`.
failure_message.example: video: The video upload failed after 5 retries.

frames_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the video frame timestamp log. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

id.description: Capture clip ID, prefixed `bclip_`.

imu_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope) log. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

manifest_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the capture manifest. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

ready_at.description: When server-side validation completed successfully, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` until then.

sequence.description: The clip's stable order within the attempt, starting at 1.

status.description: Recording and validation state. `recording` is still capturing; `verifying` is running server-side validation; `ready` passed validation and counts toward the verified-duration payout gate; `failed` did not validate.

updated_at.description: When the clip was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

video_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the synchronized MP4 video. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

items.description: The deliverable shapes this bounty accepts. Every bounty accepts any combination of `content_url` (posted links) and `media` (uploaded files), except `data_capture` bounties, whose proof is clips recorded in the Whop app that accumulate on the attempt.

accepted_submissions_limit.description: Number of submissions that can be accepted (winner slots).

accepted_submissions_per_user_limit.description: How many winner slots one worker can win. Defaults to `1`. Wins plus proofs awaiting review never exceed this number, and a worker runs one attempt at a time. Cannot exceed `accepted_submissions_limit`.

affiliate_share_amount.description: What a referrer earns per accepted submission when the worker arrived through their affiliate link, in whole currency units, at the standard platform fee rate. Taken out of the worker's post-fee reward rather than added on top. `0` when the bounty pays no affiliate share, including bounties tied to no account, which cannot record a referral.

items.description: Countries whose residents can work the bounty, as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes. Empty means worldwide.

budget_amount.description: Total gross budget committed to the bounty: `gross_reward_amount` times `accepted_submissions_limit`.

business_goal_type.description: What the poster wants the work to achieve, declared once at create. `null` for bounties created before the taxonomy rolled out.

cancel_requested_at.description: When cancellation was requested, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. On a `closed` bounty this means the cancel is pending: submissions are stopped and the bounty cancels once in-flight submissions resolve. On a `canceled` bounty it records when the cancellation was requested. `null` when no cancellation was ever requested.

created_at.description: When the bounty was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Currency for all amounts on the bounty, as a lowercase ISO 4217 code.

description.description: Full task instructions shown to workers.
description.example: Bounty Description

discussion_experience_id.description: Experience the bounty's discussion thread lives in, prefixed `exp_`. Read this — not `experience_id` — to open the thread: a platform-wide bounty has no hosting experience of its own but its discussion still lives in one.

discussion_feed_id.description: Forum feed containing the bounty's discussion thread. `null` for a bounty with no forum post.

discussion_post_id.description: Forum post anchoring the bounty's discussion thread. Read together with `discussion_experience_id` to address the thread. `null` for a bounty with no forum post.

experience_id.description: Experience the bounty is hosted in, prefixed `exp_`. `null` for platform-wide bounties; may belong to a different account than the funder.

funding_account.description: Account whose balance funds the bounty pool, or `null` when a user funds it personally. May differ from the account hosting `experience_id`.

gross_paid_out_amount.description: Gross amount paid out from the bounty pool across accepted submissions — worker payouts, platform fees, and affiliate shares together. Tips and reviewer rewards are excluded.

gross_reward_amount.description: Gross bounty-pool amount allocated per accepted submission, in whole currency units.

hosting_account.description: Account hosting the bounty's forum — the one whose `route` and `experience_id` address its discussion thread, and where its submissions dashboard lives. `null` for a platform-wide bounty with no host. May differ from `funding_account`.

id.description: Bounty ID, prefixed `bnty_`.

min_total_verified_duration_seconds.description: Total verified footage a submission must accumulate before it can be submitted, in seconds. Always a whole number of hours. Present only on `data_capture` bounties — it is what `net_reward_amount` pays for, so rate displays divide by it. `null` for every other goal type.

net_reward_amount.description: What a worker is quoted per accepted submission after the platform fee, in whole currency units. The exact post-fee figure, at the standard platform fee rate — a worker who locked a different rate, or who arrived through an affiliate link, is paid a different amount.

poster.description: User who posted the bounty — the account owner when created with an account API key.

scheduled_frequency.description: How often the schedule creates a new bounty. Each occurrence is a separate bounty; the original is not republished.

scheduled_publish_at.description: When a scheduled bounty will publish, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` once published, for bounties that were never scheduled, and for terminally failed drafts parked for manual rescheduling.

spots_remaining.description: Unfilled winner capacity: `accepted_submissions_limit` minus `accepted_submissions_count`, clamped to zero. Not on its own a signal that the bounty accepts new claims — read `status` for that: only an `open` bounty takes new submissions.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `scheduled` bounties are unpublished drafts, visible to their poster and the account's authorized managers; `open` bounties accept new submissions; `closed` bounties are live but no longer accept new submissions; `completed` bounties paid out every winner slot; `canceled` bounties ended before filling their slots.

submissions_closed_at.description: When new submissions stopped being accepted, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Set when a cancellation is requested on a bounty with work in flight, so in-flight submissions can resolve before the bounty cancels. `null` when submissions were never stopped — including completed bounties that simply filled every winner slot.

title.description: Short name of the task shown to workers.

unresolved_submissions_count.description: Submissions still awaiting an outcome: in progress or pending review.

updated_at.description: When the bounty was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

viewer_accepted_submissions_count.description: How many winner slots the authenticated user has already won on this bounty. Read against `accepted_submissions_per_user_limit` to show a worker their remaining allowance. `0` when the request has no authenticated user.

bounty_id.description: The bounty the work was submitted to, prefixed `bnty_`.

items.description: The submission's capture clips in recording order, each carrying its own review `status` and temporary signed artifact URLs. The full deliverable when `deliverable_type` is `data_capture`, populated only on single-submission reads; `null` on list responses (use `captured_clip_count` and `captured_duration_seconds` for the summary) and for other deliverable types. An attempt still in progress lists every clip it has recorded, including failed ones; once submitted, only clips that passed validation are listed, since only those are evidence.

capture_filename.description: The vendor filename stem `Country_City_Site_Station_Operator`, derived from the capture metadata. `null` until every component is present.

captured_clip_count.description: Number of verified capture clips accepted for this submission so far. `0` for submissions whose deliverable doesn't accumulate clips.

captured_duration_seconds.description: Total verified duration of accepted capture clips, in whole seconds. `0` for submissions whose deliverable doesn't accumulate clips.

city.description: Capture metadata: city the footage was recorded in. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

claimed_at.description: When the worker claimed the submission, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

content.description: Written proof the worker submitted with their work.
content.example: Ceramic coating reveal, shot at the Burnet Rd bay

country.description: Capture metadata: country the footage was recorded in. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

created_at.description: When the submission was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

deliverable_type.description: How the work arrived when it came in through the API in one shot, informational only — read the work from `deliverable_urls`, `files`, and `capture_clips` directly. `null` for submissions whose proof is a livestream recording, including ones that attached links or files on submit.

items.description: Links submitted as work, followed by temporary download URLs for the uploaded files. `null` when the submission carries neither.

denial_reason.description: Why the submission was denied, when a presentable reason exists. Always `null` unless `status` is `denied`.
denial_reason.example: The clip never shows the finished paint.

device.description: Capture metadata: device the footage was recorded on. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

items.description: Files uploaded as part of the work, in upload order. Empty when the submission has none.

fov.description: Capture metadata: horizontal field of view in degrees. `null` when not reported.

id.description: Submission ID, prefixed `btys_`.

latest_proof_livestream_feed.description: Latest public proof livestream attached to the submission.

operator.description: Capture metadata: identifier of the person who recorded the footage. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

resolved_at.description: When the submission was approved or denied, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` until then.

site.description: Capture metadata: site or venue the footage was recorded at. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

station.description: Capture metadata: station or position within the site. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `in_progress` submissions are active attempts that have not submitted proof yet; `submitted` submissions await review; `approved` submissions were accepted and paid; `denied` submissions were rejected. `null` when the attempt ended without proof, taking it out of the public lifecycle — those attempts are absent from every public list and read.

submitted_at.description: When proof was submitted for review, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` while the attempt is in progress.

updated_at.description: When the submission was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

content_type.description: MIME type of the file.

filename.description: Name the file was uploaded with.

id.description: File ID, prefixed `file_`.

url.description: Temporary download URL for the file.

ended_at.description: When the proof livestream ended, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` while it is still live — a feed with a `started_at` and no `ended_at` is streaming right now.

id.description: Livestream feed ID.

recording_url.description: Playback URL for a completed proof recording, when available.

started_at.description: When the proof livestream went live, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` before it starts.

thumbnail_url.description: Current proof thumbnail URL, when available.

title.description: Display title for the proof livestream.

BusinessGoalTypes.description: What the poster is trying to accomplish with a workforce bounty. Used for product taxonomy and analytics, separate from the bounty's implementation type.

CancelOptions.description: The different reasons a user can choose for why they are canceling their membership.

CancelationStatus.description: The state of a membership after a customer provides a cancelation reason.

filename_pattern.description: The naming convention for uploaded files, built from the required metadata fields.

manifest_schema_version.description: Schema version the client must stamp on the capture manifest it uploads.

min_clip_duration_seconds.description: Minimum length of a single clip, in seconds.

min_total_verified_duration_seconds.description: Total verified footage a submission must accumulate across all its clips before it can be submitted, in seconds. Always a whole number of hours.

items.description: Metadata fields a submission must provide, matching the `metadata` object on the submissions API.

single_continuous_take.description: Whether each clip must be one uninterrupted recording rather than stitched segments.

device_motion_units.description: Units for the device-motion channels, as a compact key=unit string.

min_rate_hz.description: Minimum sustained IMU sample rate in hertz for a clip to pass validation.

target_rate_hz.description: Target IMU sample rate in hertz.

warmup_min_rate_hz.description: Minimum IMU sample rate in hertz tolerated during the warmup window.

warmup_ns.description: Startup window, in nanoseconds, during which the relaxed warmup rate applies.

bitrate_ceiling_mbps.description: Maximum acceptable average bitrate, in megabits per second.

bitrate_floor_mbps.description: Minimum acceptable average bitrate, in megabits per second.

bitrate_target_mbps.description: Recommended average bitrate to encode at, in megabits per second.

camera_lens.description: Which physical lens to record with.

items.description: Accepted video codecs, in preference order.

embed_camera_metadata.description: Whether the client must also write the camera make and model into the video container's metadata. When `false`, the capture manifest and export CSV are the metadata carrier.

frame_gap_tolerance_ms.description: Longest stall between consecutive frames a clip may contain before the client rejects it, in milliseconds. Every frame is timestamped in the frame log, so a stall stays alignable downstream — this bounds how broken a capture may be, not how evenly it must be paced.

height.description: Required frame height in pixels — recorded footage must match exactly.

min_fov_degrees.description: Minimum acceptable horizontal field of view, in degrees.

preferred_fov_degrees.description: Preferred horizontal field of view, in degrees.

stabilization_mode.description: How the client must configure video stabilization: `off` disables EIS so raw motion is preserved for pose extraction, `on` requires it, `any` leaves the device default.

stabilization_required.description: Whether hardware/software stabilization must be enabled. True exactly when stabilization_mode is `on`.

width.description: Required frame width in pixels — recorded footage must match exactly.

usd_amount.description: Amount charged in USD. Negative when the merchant refunded the card.

account_id.description: Connected account filter from the request, prefixed `biz_`. Omitted when not supplied.

cashback_rule_id.description: Cashback rule filter from the request, prefixed `cicbr_`. Omitted when not supplied.

status.description: Request status. `processing` means background processing was queued, not that payment completed. `failed`, returned with HTTP `200`, means the queue rejected the request. Subsequent transaction failures retry automatically.

created_at.description: When the rule was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

description.description: Optional description of the cashback rule.
description.example: Cloud cashback

discarded_at.description: When the rule was discarded, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Null means it has not been discarded.

expires_at.description: Exclusive end of the eligibility window, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Null means no expiration.

funding_account_id.description: Platform account designated to fund cashback, prefixed `biz_`. Derived from the authenticated credential.

id.description: Cashback rule ID, prefixed `cicbr_`.

merchant_category_code.description: Four-digit merchant category code. Null matches any MCC. When both merchant filters are null, scoped_account_id is required.

merchant_name.description: Raw merchant name reported by the card provider. Null matches any merchant name. When set, matches together with any MCC filter; not a substring or enriched display-name match.

rate_bps.description: Cashback rate in basis points. 100 means 1%, and 10000 means 100%.

scoped_account_id.description: Connected account ID, prefixed `biz_`. Null designates all direct connected accounts of the funding platform.

starts_at.description: Inclusive start of the rule's eligibility window, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

updated_at.description: When the rule was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

ChatChannel.description: A real-time chat feed attached to an experience, with configurable moderation and posting permissions.

ban_media.description: Whether media uploads such as images and videos are blocked in this chat.

ban_urls.description: Whether URL links are blocked from being posted in this chat.

banned_words.description: A list of words that are automatically filtered from messages in this chat. Empty unless the caller has permission to moderate this chat.

items.description: Represents textual data as UTF-8 character sequences. This type is most often used by GraphQL to represent free-form human-readable text.

experience.description: The experience this chat feed is attached to.

id.description: The unique identifier for the experience.

name.description: The display name of this experience shown to users in the product navigation. Maximum 255 characters.

user_posts_cooldown_seconds.description: The minimum number of seconds a user must wait between consecutive messages. Null if no cooldown is enforced.

who_can_post.description: The permission level controlling which users can send messages in this chat.

who_can_react.description: The permission level controlling which users can add reactions in this chat.

account_id.description: Account ID, prefixed `biz_`.

affiliate_code.description: Affiliate code applied at checkout, or `null` when none is set.

created_at.description: When the checkout configuration was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Currency used for setup-mode payment method availability; defaults to `usd` when omitted.

effective_payment_method_configuration.description: The configuration governing a checkout mounted from this configuration, resolved through every layer (its own overrides, the variant's, and the account's) — the shape a session's `payment_method_configuration` carries. Apply it over the payment method types catalogue for the offerable set. `null` means platform defaults; `payment_method_configuration` stays this configuration's own editable override.

metadata.description: Custom key-value metadata copied to payments and memberships. `null` without the `checkout_configuration:basic:read` scope.

mode.description: Controls whether checkout charges the buyer immediately or saves payment details for later.

payment_method_configuration.description: Payment method overrides for this checkout. `null` when it uses the variant or platform defaults.

purchase_url.description: Checkout URL you can send to customers.

redirect_url.description: URL customers are sent to after checkout, or `null` when no redirect is configured.

three_ds_level.description: 3D Secure behavior for supported on-session card payments. `mandate_challenge` requires a 3DS challenge before payment processing; `mandate_if_required` mandates a challenge only when the payment processor requires it; `frictionless_if_required` uses the regular frictionless 3DS flow. Payments of $1,000 or more use `mandate_if_required` unless `mandate_challenge` is selected. Risk and authentication recovery requirements can override the preference. Applies in setup mode; `null` uses frictionless 3DS. Payment mode uses the variant policy.

updated_at.description: When the checkout configuration was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

variant.description: Variant used for payment checkout. `null` in setup mode.

CheckoutConfigurationListItem.description: A checkout configuration is a reusable configuration for a checkout, including the plan, affiliate, and custom metadata. Payments and memberships created from a checkout session inherit its metadata.

account_id.description: The ID of the account to use for the checkout configuration

affiliate_code.description: The affiliate code to use for the checkout configuration

company_id.description: The ID of the account to use for the checkout configuration

currency.description: The currency to use for the configuration when in 'setup' mode. This is used to target which currency specific payment methods are available. If not provided, it will default to 'usd' when in setup mode.

id.description: The unique identifier for the checkout session.

metadata.description: The metadata to use for the checkout configuration

mode.description: The mode of the checkout session.

payment_method_configuration.description: The explicit payment method configuration for the session, if any. This currently only works in 'setup' mode. Use the plan's payment_method_configuration for payment method.

disabled.description: An array of payment method identifiers that are explicitly disabled. Only applies if the include_platform_defaults is true.

enabled.description: An array of payment method identifiers that are explicitly enabled. This means these payment methods will be shown on checkout. Example use case is to only enable a specific payment method like cashapp, or extending the platform defaults with additional methods.

include_platform_defaults.description: Whether Whop's platform default payment method enablement settings are included in this configuration. The full list of default payment methods can be found in the documentation at docs.whop.com/payments.

plan.description: The plan to use for the checkout configuration

adaptive_pricing_enabled.description: Whether the creator has turned on adaptive pricing for this plan. Raw setting — does not check processor compatibility or feature flags.

billing_period.description: Number of days between recurring charges, such as 30 for monthly or 365 for annual. `null` for one-time plans.

currency.description: The currency used for all prices on this plan (e.g., 'usd', 'eur'). All monetary amounts on the plan are denominated in this currency.

expiration_days.description: Access duration in days for expiration-based plans, such as 365 for a one-year pass.

id.description: The unique identifier for the plan.

initial_price.description: The initial purchase price in the plan's base_currency (e.g., 49.99 for $49.99). For one-time plans, this is the full price. For renewal plans, this is charged on top of the first renewal_price.

plan_type.description: The billing model for this plan: 'renewal' for recurring subscriptions or 'one_time' for single payments.

release_method.description: Sales method for this plan: `buy_now` for immediate purchase or `waitlist` for waitlist-based access.

renewal_price.description: The recurring price charged every billing_period in the plan's base_currency (e.g., 9.99 for $9.99/period). Zero for one-time plans.

three_ds_level.description: The 3D Secure behavior for this plan. Null means the plan inherits the account default.

trial_period_days.description: Free trial days before first renewal charge. `null` if no trial is configured or the user has already used a trial for this plan.

visibility.description: Controls whether the plan is visible to customers. When set to 'hidden', the plan is only accessible via direct link.

purchase_url.description: A URL you can send to customers to complete a checkout. It looks like `/checkout/ch_xxxx/`

redirect_url.description: The URL to redirect the user to after the checkout configuration is created

adaptive_pricing_enabled.description: Whether this variant accepts local currency payments via adaptive pricing.

billing_period.description: Recurring billing interval in days.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code for the variant's prices.

expiration_days.description: Access duration in days for expiration-based variants.

id.description: Variant ID, prefixed `plan_`.

initial_price.description: Initial purchase price in the variant currency.

renewal_price.description: Recurring price charged each billing period.

three_ds_level.description: 3D Secure behavior for supported on-session card payments. `mandate_challenge` requires a 3DS challenge before payment processing; `mandate_if_required` mandates a challenge only when the payment processor requires it; `frictionless_if_required` uses the regular frictionless 3DS flow. Payments of $1,000 or more use `mandate_if_required` unless `mandate_challenge` is selected. Risk and authentication recovery requirements can override the preference. `null` inherits the account default.

trial_period_days.description: Free trial days before the first renewal charge.

visibility.description: Whether the variant is visible to customers or hidden from public view.

CheckoutFonts.description: The different font families available for checkout pages.

CheckoutModes.description: The different modes a checkout can be set to.

items.description: Payment methods this checkout withholds, even when the defaults would offer them.
Payment methods this checkout offers on top of whatever the defaults provide.

include_platform_defaults.description: Whether Whop's default set is the starting point. When `false`, only `enabled` is offered.

CheckoutShapes.description: The different border-radius styles available for checkout pages.

company.description: The company whose token balance this transaction affects.

id.description: The unique identifier for the company.

route.description: The slug/route of the company on the Whop site.

title.description: The written name of the company.

member.description: The member whose token balance was affected by this transaction.

user.description: The user whose token balance was affected by this transaction.

name.description: The user's display name shown on their public profile.

username.description: The user's unique username shown on their public profile.

acceptable.description: Whether the dispute can be conceded to the customer with `POST /disputes/{id}/accept`. True only for a chargeback still awaiting a response, before `evidence_due_at`, whose payment processor supports accepting disputes. Inquiries are never acceptable.

account_id.description: The account the dispute was filed against, prefixed `biz_`.

amount.description: The disputed amount, in whole units of `currency`.

buyer.description: The customer who filed the dispute.

created_at.description: When the dispute was opened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code of the disputed amount.

evidence.description: The evidence packet sent to the processor to contest the dispute.

evidence_due_at.description: The deadline to submit evidence, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` when the network already auto-resolved the dispute (Visa RDR) with no evidence round, or when the processor hasn't reported a deadline for this dispute.

evidence_editable.description: Whether `evidence` can still be changed and submitted.

evidence_locked_reason.description: Why evidence can no longer be edited. `null` while `evidence_editable` is true.

evidence_submitted_at.description: When the evidence was submitted to the processor, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

fee.description: The dispute fee charged to the seller, in the currency it was collected in. `null` when no fee was charged, such as for an inquiry or a Visa RDR resolution.

id.description: Dispute ID, prefixed `dspt_`.

inquiry.description: Whether this is a pre-dispute inquiry rather than a formal chargeback. Inquiries follow the same lifecycle but move no funds unless one escalates.

items.description: What the card issuer said when filing the dispute. Only populated when the issuer provides them, and listed in the order they were received.

Everything the disputed payment charged for, in purchase order. `product_id` and `variant_id` name the first of these; a cart's later items appear only here. A payment made before items were recorded lists the single item its variant implies. Empty when the payment is not linked to a variant.

product_id.description: The product the disputed payment was for, prefixed `prod_`.

reason.description: Why the customer says they are disputing, normalized across processors and card networks. `other` covers a processor reason Whop has not categorized yet.

reason_code.description: The raw card-network or processor reason code, such as `10.4`. Informational only — `reason` is not derived from it.

status.description: Where the dispute stands. `needs_response` is awaiting evidence, `under_review` is with the processor, `won` returned the funds to the seller, `lost` returned them to the customer, and `prevented` means the customer was refunded before any ruling, so it settles like `lost`. The `warning_` statuses are the same stages for an inquiry, which moves no funds. A dispute past its `evidence_due_at` reports `under_review` — the window to respond has closed.

updated_at.description: When the dispute was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

variant_id.description: The variant the disputed payment was made on, prefixed `plan_`.

account_id.description: The account the alerted payment belongs to, prefixed `biz_`. `null` while the alert is unmatched.

amount.description: The alerted amount, in whole units of `currency`. This is what the issuer reported, which can differ from the payment's own amount.

auto_refunded.description: Whether Whop automatically refunded the alerted payment. Reflects the payment, so it can be `true` for a refund issued by another flow (RDR, resolution) on the same payment.

card_brand.description: The card network as reported by the issuer, lowercased, such as `visa` or `mastercard`. `unknown` when the report carries neither a network nor a recognizable BIN.

category.description: What the cardholder claims. `fraud` when they say they didn't make the payment: always for an `early_fraud_warning`, and for Ethoca fraud alerts and Visa RDR cases filed under a fraud reason. `customer_dispute` when they made the payment but dispute it, such as a product not received or a canceled subscription. `null` when the alert carries no claim, such as an issuer's request for transaction documents.

created_at.description: When Whop received the alert, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code of the alerted amount.

fee.description: The alert fee charged to the account, in the currency it was collected in. `null` when `fee_charged` is false.

fee_charged.description: Whether Whop charged the account an alert fee for this one. Always `false` for `early_fraud_warning`, which Whop is not billed for and never passes on.

id.description: Dispute alert ID, prefixed `dspa_`.

issuer.description:
Deprecated: always `null` outside Whop's own dashboard. Name of the bank that issued the card and filed the report.
DEPRECATED: Always null outside Whop's own dashboard.

payment_id.description: The payment the issuer reported, prefixed `pay_`. `null` when Whop could not match the report to a payment.

product_id.description: The product the alerted payment was for, prefixed `prod_`.

reported_at.description: When the issuer filed the report, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Earlier than `created_at`, which is when Whop received it.

source.description: The network program that sent the alert, which `type` alone doesn't tell apart. `ethoca` for Mastercard Ethoca, `cdrn` for Visa Verifi CDRN, `rdr` for Visa RDR, `tc40` / `safe` for a Visa / Mastercard fraud report, `paypal` for a PayPal alert. `null` when the network didn't say.

transaction_at.description: When the reported transaction was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp — falls back to when the matched payment was made if the issuer's own report didn't carry one. Should not be `null` in practice; treat one as a data issue rather than expected behavior.

type.description: What the issuer sent. `early_fraud_warning` is a fraud report on a settled payment (Visa TC40 / Mastercard SAFE) — refunding still avoids the chargeback, and Whop never charges a fee for one. `dispute_alert` is a pre-dispute notice from the issuer's alert network, which Whop pays for and passes on as a fee. `rapid_dispute_resolution` is a Visa RDR case the network already closed by refunding the payment — nothing is left to act on.

updated_at.description: When the alert was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

contact_url.description: A web form for contacting the registrant, published when the registrar withholds their email. `null` when there is none.

country.description: Registrant country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, such as `US`, or `null` when withheld.

email.description: Registrant email address, often a privacy forwarding address, or `null` when withheld.

name.description: Registrant name, or `null` when withheld.

organization.description: Registrant organization, often a privacy service, or `null` when withheld.

phone.description: Registrant phone number, or `null` when withheld.

iana_id.description: The registrar's IANA registrar ID, or `null` when the record omits it.

name.description: Registrar name, such as `GoDaddy.com, LLC`.

url.description: The registrar's website, or `null` when the record omits it.

amount_due.description: What the domain owes now. `null` when nothing is owed.

auto_renew.description: Whether Whop charges the saved payment method to renew the domain before it expires.

expires_at.description: When the registration expires unless renewed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` until it's registered.

method.description: How the domain came to Whop: `registration` when it was bought through Whop, `transfer` when it was moved from another registrar.

payment_method_id.description: ID of the saved card charged for the domain, prefixed `payt_`. `null` when none is set.

phase.description: Where the registration is: awaiting payment, ordering at the registrar, transferring from another registrar, delegating DNS to Whop, held, expired, or releasing.

purchase_url.description: Link to pay what the domain owes now: its registration or transfer, or a yearly renewal. `null` when nothing is owed.

renewal_price.description: What each yearly renewal costs at the registrar's current price. Set when the response is a single domain; `null` in lists, while the domain is being released, or when the price can't be read right now.

state.description: How far registering and keeping the domain has got.

unique_visitors_last_7_days.description: People who viewed a page on the domain with the Whop pixel in the last 7 days, refreshed hourly.

code.description: The code that takes the domain. For an `internal` move it starts `whop_dt_`, and the receiving Whop account enters it as `registration.auth_code` when it creates or updates the domain. Returned when the response is a single domain and you can manage it; `null` otherwise.

destination.description: Where the domain is moving. `internal` is another Whop account.

state.description: `ready` while the code waits to be used. `pending` once it has: Whop removes the domain's email, Apple Pay and pixel from this account, then moves the registration and removes the domain from this account.
How far proving verification has got.

verification_expires_at.description: When an unproven claim is removed, 48 hours after it was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

app.description: The app the domain serves. `null` until you choose one; the domain shows a placeholder page meanwhile.

state.description: How far serving the website has got.

base_url.description: The production base URL where the app is hosted. `null` if no base URL is configured or the domain isn't yours.

id.description: App ID, prefixed `app_`.

account_id.description: ID of the account this recommendation is for, prefixed `biz_`, or null for personal onboarding.

acknowledged_at.description: When the executed run was first marked as seen, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` if it has not been.

action_type.description: Type of action recommended, or `null` when no type is assigned. New values may be added; handle unknown types gracefully.

ai_chat_id.description: The chat that ran the recommendation, shown only to the user who ran it, or `null` otherwise.

created_at.description: When the recommendation was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or null for an unsaved recommendation.

executed_at.description: When the recommendation was carried out, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` if it has not been.

items.description: Expected API operations or tools, in execution order, or null when no execution plan was recorded.

id.description: Recommendation ID, prefixed `reca_`, or `create_business` for an unsaved setup recommendation. Authenticate and list again before executing an unsaved recommendation.

input.description: What you requested, in your own words, or `null` for recommendations generated without your input.

items.description: Decisions this recommendation leaves to you. Pick one option for each before it runs, or write your own for a `whop_ai` recommendation; empty when there is nothing to decide.

prompt.description: Step-by-step instructions for Whop AI, or `null` when no instructions are available.
prompt.example: Create a 20% off promo code for my members.

reasoning.description: Evidence and metrics supporting the recommendation, or `null` when no reasoning was provided.

result_url.description: Where to view what the run produced, such as the published website or created product, or `null` when the result is only in the chat.

run_by_user_id.description: The user who started the run, prefixed `user_`, or `null` if it has not run or was started without a user, such as with an API key.

run_ended_at.description: When the run ended, whether executed or incomplete, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` if it has not ended.

run_started_at.description: When the run started, by Whop AI or the recommendation's API calls, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` if it has not run.

sentiment.description: How the user rated this recommendation, or `null` if they have not rated it

status.description: `queued` when awaiting generation; `pending` while generating; `ready` when available to run; `running` while Whop AI or the recommendation's API calls carry it out; `executed` when carried out; `incomplete` when the run ended without carrying it out; `superseded` when rejected or replaced.

superseded_at.description: When the recommendation was rejected or replaced, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` if neither has occurred.

target_url.description: Website URL selected for pixel setup, or `null` when no website was captured for this recommendation.

title.description: Recommended action and its expected benefit, or `null` until generated.
title.example: Move $180 from 3 dead ad groups into BATCH#3, +1.7x return

user_feedback.description: The user's written feedback, or `null` if they have not provided any.

answer.description: What the run used: one of the options, or your own text for a `whop_ai` recommendation. `null` until a run starts.

id.description: Identifies the input when you answer it.

label.description: What you are choosing, such as the daily ad budget.

items.description: Three suggested values, strongest first. You can answer with one of them, or with your own text for a `whop_ai` recommendation.

template.description: A plan sentence with one {answer} blank to fill with the selected answer.

description.description: Concise description of the operation and affected resource, or null for older recommendations.
description.example: Increase the summer campaign budget

tool_name.description: API operation or assistant tool name.

account_id.description: ID of the account the address belongs to, prefixed `biz_`.

address.description: The full address in lowercase, such as support@example.com.

created_at.description: When the address was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

domain_id.description: ID of the domain the address is on, prefixed `dom_`.

id.description: Email address ID, prefixed `emaddr_`.

password.description: The password mail apps sign in to the mailbox with over IMAP and SMTP, using the address as the username. `null` unless you can use the mailbox: you own it, or nobody owns it and you have `email:read` and `email:send`.

updated_at.description: When the address was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

user_id.description: ID of the team member who owns the mailbox, prefixed `user_`. Only they can read it or send from it. `null` when the whole account shares it.

EmbedTypes.description: The type of embed for a lesson

custom_field_responses.description: The list of responses collected from the user when submitting their waitlist entry.

product.description: The product associated with this entry's waitlisted plan. Null if the plan is not tied to a product.

title.description: The display name of the product shown to customers on the product page and in search results.

status.description: The current status of the waitlist entry (e.g., drafted, pending, approved, denied).

user.description: The user who submitted this waitlist entry.

email.description: The user's email address. Requires the member:email:read permission to access. Null if not authorized.

name.description: The user's display name shown on their public profile.

username.description: The user's unique username shown on their public profile.

EntryStatus.description: The status of an entry to a waitlist.

icon.description: The icon image for this app, displayed on the app store, product pages, checkout, and as the default icon for experiences using this app.

url.description: A pre-optimized URL for rendering this attachment on the client. This should be used for displaying attachments in apps.

company.description: The company that owns this experience.

route.description: URL slug for the account's store page, e.g. `pickaxe` in whop.com/pickaxe.

id.description: The unique identifier for the experience.

image.description: The custom logo image for this experience. Null if no custom logo has been uploaded.

url.description: A pre-optimized URL for rendering this attachment on the client. This should be used for displaying attachments in apps.

name.description: The display name of this experience shown to users in the product navigation. Maximum 255 characters.

order.description: The sort position of this experience within its section. Lower values appear first. Null if no position has been set.

products.description: The list of products this experience is attached to, which determines which customers have access. Empty if the experience is only visible to authorized company team members.

items.description: A product is a digital good or service sold on Whop. Products contain plans for pricing and experiences for content delivery.

id.description: The unique identifier for the product.

route.description: URL slug in the product's public link, e.g. `pickaxe-analytics` in whop.com/company/pickaxe-analytics.

level.description: What the user is notified about in the experience: `all` notifications, only `mentions`, or `nothing`.

scope.description: What the preference applies to. Echo it back to `PATCH /users/me/preferences/notifications` to change this preference.

account_id.description: Owning account ID.

assignment_seed.description: Assignment hashes UTF-8 seed + subject ID with CRC32 modulo 100 and selects the stored end-exclusive range.

bucket_by.description: Randomization unit — `user` buckets each user independently, `account` buckets whole accounts (every user of an account gets the same arm). `null` for feature flags.

configuration_revision.description: Revision of the serving configuration. Increments on every configuration change, so a cached definition with a lower revision is stale. Does not change the assignment seed.

created_at.description: When the experiment was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

created_by.description: ID of the user who created the experiment, prefixed `user_`. `null` for experiments created before creators were recorded.

ended_at.description: When the experiment stopped collecting data, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` while still running.

feature_flag_only.description: `true` when this was created as a feature flag rather than a full experiment. Feature flags share the same evaluation API but do not collect metric results.

findings.description: What was learned and why this outcome, recorded when the experiment was ended. `null` until then.

flag_key.description: Developer-chosen handle referenced from code. Anywhere the API takes an experiment identifier, the `expt_` id and the flag_key are interchangeable.

hypothesis.description: Hypothesis for this experiment. `null` when none is set, and always `null` for feature flags.

id.description: Unique identifier for the experiment, prefixed `expt_`.

name.description: Human-readable display name.

related_resource.description: Resource owned by the account that this experiment is bound to, such as an app or product. `null` when unbound. Fixed once the experiment first activates.

started_at.description: When the experiment began collecting data, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` for drafts.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `draft` — not yet live; `active` — currently running; `paused` — traffic paused; `ended` — concluded.

targeting_rules.description: Rules gating who is in the experiment at all. Conditions within a rule are AND-ed, rules are OR-ed, and `exclude` rules always win. Empty means everyone qualifies.

conditions.description: Conditions within this rule, all of which must match.

field.description: Property name to read from the user context. Present when `type` is `property`.

type.description: What the condition matches on: the user ID, the account ID, or a named user property.

value.description: Value or list of values to match against.

type.description: `include` — users matching this rule qualify; `exclude` — users matching this rule are always excluded, overriding any include rule.

variants.description: Treatment arms. Users outside every arm's allocation form the implicit `control` group. Weights only ever grow and arms are never removed, so a user moves from control into a treatment at most once.

name.description: Treatment identifier. `control` is reserved — it is the implicit remainder.

ranges.description: Granted bucket ranges (1% units, end-exclusive) recording this arm's allocation history. Server-managed; ranges are only ever appended, which is what keeps assignments permanent.

weight.description: Percentage of all users assigned to this treatment, 1–100. All weights together sum to at most 100; the remainder is control.

winning_arm.description: The treatment that won, set when the experiment was ended. Once set, every evaluation returns this arm to every caller regardless of targeting or allocation, and no further exposures are recorded. `null` means control won — an ended experiment with no winning arm evaluates to `control` for everyone. Always `null` for feature flags, which simply evaluate to disabled once ended.

enabled.description: Whether the subject receives a treatment or enabled feature flag.

experiment_id.description: Unique experiment ID, included for account experiments.

flag_key.description: Present when evaluating a single experiment.

variant.description: Treatment name, control, or null for an inactive flag or excluded subject.

id.description: Referenced resource tag, belonging to the experiment owner.

created_at.description: When the export was requested, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

download_url.description: A short-lived link to download the finished file. `null` until `status` is `completed`, and again once the export has expired.

expires_at.description: When the file is deleted and the export moves to `expired`, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Exports are retained for 30 days.

id.description: Export ID, prefixed `exprt_`.

resource.description: The resource that was exported, e.g. `receipts`, `members`, or `payouts`.

status.description: `pending` or `processing` while the file is generated, `completed` when the download is ready, `failed` if it errored, `expired` once the file has been deleted.

updated_at.description: When the export last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

error.description: Why this external account currently can't be used for advertising — a failed share or a Meta-side restriction. Null when the account is healthy.
error.example: You don't have permission to share this account. Ask an admin of its Meta Business Portfolio to grant you full control, then share it again.

external_id.description: The platform-specific ID for this external account.

id.description: Unique identifier for the external account.

name.description: The display name of the external account on the platform.

parent_external_account.description: The external account this one belongs to on the platform, such as the Facebook page that owns an Instagram account. Null when the external account stands on its own, or when it is a partner.

partnership_status.description: Where a partner creator's permission to run partnership ads stands. `pending` until the creator approves it in the Instagram app, `approved` once they have, and `revoked` once it no longer holds. Null when the external account isn't a partner.

platform.description: The platform the external account exists on.

profile_picture_url.description: The URL where the profile picture of the external account can be accessed.

items.description: Capabilities Whop retains specific to this external account. For example, Whop may request the ability to run advertisements that use this external account's identity, reflected by `advertise`. Personal profile connections have no additional Whop scopes.

url.description: The URL where the external account can be accessed on the platform. Null while a Whop-owned account is still being provisioned.

username.description: The username of the external account on the platform. Null while a Whop-owned account is still being provisioned, and on platforms without usernames, such as Klaviyo.

verified.description: Whether the external account is verified on the platform.

completion.description: Screen shown after the form is submitted. `null` when the form has none.

created_at.description: When the form was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

disclaimer.description: Custom consent disclaimer shown before submission. `null` when the form has none.

form_type.description: `more_volume` is quickest to submit; `higher_intent` adds a confirmation step before submission.

id.description: The ad platform's identifier for the form. Use it as lead_gen_form_id on an ad to reuse the form.

intro.description: Intro screen shown before the questions. `null` when the form has none.

locale.description: Language the form is shown in, such as en_US.

name.description: Advertiser-facing form name.

privacy_policy_link_text.description: Custom link text for the privacy policy. `null` when the default is used.

privacy_policy_url.description: Privacy policy URL configured on the form.

items.description: Labels of the questions the form asks, for preview.
Questions on the form, in order.

profile_picture_url.description: The URL where the profile picture of the parent external account can be accessed.

username.description: The username of the parent external account on the platform.

verified.description: Whether the parent external account is verified on the platform.

call_to_action.description: The post's call-to-action button, for example shop_now (Facebook only; null for Instagram and TikTok).

caption.description: The text accompanying the post, when available.

destination_url.description: The URL the post's call-to-action drives to (Facebook only; null for Instagram and TikTok).

embed_url.description: An iframe-embeddable URL for previewing the post inline (the platform's player or post embed). For TikTok this is the only preview, since media_url is null; for Facebook and Instagram it supplements media_url. Null when no public embed is available.

id.description: The platform's own identifier for the post or media. Use it to reference the post on an ad.

media_url.description: The URL of the post's media — the image for image posts, the playable video file for video posts. Null for TikTok, which exposes no raw file (use embed_url). Meta URLs are signed and expire after roughly 24 hours, so don't store them.

items.description: Ways this post can't be used on an ad. `lead_form_ineligible`: post can't be used in lead form ads. `promotion_ineligible`: the platform won't promote this post at all — always present when that's true, alongside a reason code when one is identified. `copyrighted_music`: post uses music the platform does not allow for ads. `messenger_destination`, `instagram_destination`, `whatsapp_destination`: the post's own button opens that chat app, so the post can only run in an ad group that sends people to the same one — always accompanied by `lead_form_ineligible`. Empty when the post has no restrictions.

thumbnail_url.description: Poster image for video posts (always set for TikTok, which is video-only); null for image posts, where media_url is already the image.

video_id.description: The platform video identifier for engagement audience rules. Null for non-video posts or when unavailable. Facebook video identifiers differ from post identifiers.

category.description: The category saved as the membership's `cancel_option` when a member picks this option.

blurhash.description: BlurHash placeholder for an image or video. Null when unavailable or removed by moderation.

content_type.description: The original file's MIME type, preserved when removed by moderation, e.g. `application/pdf`.

created_at.description: When the file was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

duration_seconds.description: Audio or video duration in seconds. Null when unavailable or removed by moderation.

filename.description: The original filename, including its extension.

height.description: Image or video height in pixels. Null when unavailable or removed by moderation.

id.description: The file's ID, prefixed `file_`.

multipart_chunk_size.description: The byte size each part (except the last) must be. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

multipart_upload_id.description: The ID of the multipart upload, passed back to `complete`. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

items.description: The presigned URL for each part. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

object.description: The type of this object, always `file`.

removed_by_moderation.description: Whether moderation removed the file. When true, `url` serves a replacement image; filename, size, and content type still describe the original file.

size.description: The file size in bytes. `null` until the upload has finished.

upload_headers.description: Headers to send with the upload PUT. Present only on create.

upload_status.description: Where the file is in its upload lifecycle.

upload_url.description: Presigned URL to PUT the file's bytes to. Present only on create, and only for single-part uploads.

url.description: A URL to download the file: a permanent CDN URL for public files, a signed expiring URL for private ones. Null until the upload has finished; a replacement image URL when removed by moderation.

visibility.description: `public` files are served via an unsigned CDN URL; `private` files via a signed, expiring URL.

waveform_url.description: Audio waveform URL. Null when unavailable or removed by moderation.

width.description: Image or video width in pixels. Null when unavailable or removed by moderation.

part_number.description: The 1-based index of this part within the multipart upload.

url.description: The presigned URL to PUT this part's bytes to.

FileVisibility.description: Controls whether an uploaded file is publicly accessible or requires authentication to access.

account_id.description: The merchant account whose financing access changed, prefixed biz_.

disabled_at.description: When the payment methods were disabled, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

items.description: BNPL payment methods disabled on this account.

provider.description: The BNPL provider whose dispute rate triggered enforcement. Other payment methods may also lose access.

account_id.description: The ID of the merchant account applying for payment financing, starting with biz_.

created_at.description: When the application was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

feedback.description: Public review feedback when more information is requested or the application is denied. Internal notes are never included.

id.description: The financing application ID, starting with inrq_.

items.description: Merchant requirements and saved answers. Present on individual application responses, omitted from lists. Acceptance is collected separately on submit.

status.description: The application's review state. Approval does not by itself indicate that financing payment methods are enabled on the account.

terms.description: Current terms to present before submitting. Present on individual application responses.

updated_at.description: When the application was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

action.description: The merchant action that turns this provider on when `status` is `needs_action`; `null` otherwise.

items.description: The currencies checkout charges this provider in for this account, each with its maximum payment.

details.description: The dispute rates behind a `dispute_rate_near_limit` or `dispute_rate_exceeded` reason; `null` for every other reason.

provider_reviewed_at.description: When the provider received or decided on this account, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Set only for providers that review merchants themselves (Splitit); `null` otherwise.

reason.description: Why the provider has this status, when known. On `active` it is `dispute_rate_near_limit` when the provider is close to being turned off. On `inactive` it names what keeps it off, including `not_included` when the account's approval doesn't cover it, `turned_off` when it was switched off after setup, `setup_failed`, and `declined` when the provider turned the account down without a reason Whop recognizes. More reasons may be added.

status.description: Where the provider stands for this account: `eligible` (included if the account applies), `needs_action` (waiting on the merchant, see `action`), `in_review` (waiting on Whop's review, or on the provider's own when `reason` is `provider_review`), `active` (offered at checkout), or `inactive` (not offered, see `reason`).

currency.description: A currency checkout charges this provider in, lowercase ISO 4217.

max_amount.description: The largest payment checkout offers this provider for in this currency. Null when checkout sets no maximum, or when the provider sets each merchant's limit itself (Splitit).

dispute_rate.description: The account's dispute rate as a fraction, for example 0.012 for 1.2%.

dispute_rate_limit.description: The dispute rate, as a fraction, at which the provider is turned off or held back.

source_provider.description: The provider whose dispute rate caused this change, or `null` when it was this provider's own rate.

items.description: Accepted document formats, such as pdf or jpeg.

field.description: The information requested, such as business_description or processing_statements.

file_collection_type.description: Whether the requirement accepts no file, one file, or multiple files.

items.description: Files attached to this requirement, including expiring download URLs.

id.description: Requirement ID to use when updating this application's answers.

max_file_size.description: Maximum size in bytes for each uploaded document.

minimum_length.description: Minimum characters per text answer, when specified.

money.description: Saved maximum product price in its original currency. Null when unanswered or the saved legacy answer is invalid.

items.description: Allowed dropdown values. Empty when the answer is not an enumeration.

required.description: Whether this requirement must be completed before submission.

text_collection_type.description: Whether the requirement accepts no text, one value, or multiple values.

text_format.description: Expected text format. max_product_price uses money instead of values.

items.description: Saved text answers. Empty for money requirements; read money instead.
