post.description:
Adds a domain to your account with the capabilities you want.

Pass `registration` to buy the domain through Whop; it's the default when you pass no capability. Pay its `amount_due` at `purchase_url`, or pass `registration.payment_method_id` to charge a saved card. Whop then registers it, runs its DNS, and renews it every year while `auto_renew` is on.

Pass `registration.auth_code` to transfer in a domain you own at another registrar. The transfer starts once its `amount_due` is paid, or at once when `amount_due` is `null`. While `registration.phase` is `transferring`, its `issues` say what the transfer needs from you.

Pass `verification` to connect a domain you registered elsewhere: its `issues` list the TXT and routing records to publish. Pass `website` with an `app_id` to serve that app on the domain.

To change a domain you already have, update it instead. Adding a domain this account deleted revives it under its original ID.

account_id.description: Account ID, prefixed biz_. Required for user credentials; otherwise defaults to the credential's account.

apple_pay.description: Accept Apple Pay at checkout on the domain. It needs no other capability. Whop registers the domain with Apple: it stays `pending` until Apple answers, then turns `ready`, or `action_required` when Apple couldn't fetch the domain association file. Serve the file, then check the domain to register it again. Pass `null` to turn Apple Pay off: Whop removes the domain from Apple, and the domain stays, like releasing any other capability.

domain.description: Bare hostname, such as example.com or checkout.example.com. A bought domain must be a root domain. Wildcards, paths, schemes, and ports are not accepted.

email.description: Send and receive email on the domain. Only a domain bought through Whop, or a subdomain of one in the same account, can have it. Whop publishes the DNS records and stays `pending` until its email provider verifies them, then turns `ready`. Pass `null` to remove email.

metadata.description: Custom string keys and values.

pixel.description: Track page views on the domain with the Whop pixel. It needs no other capability: it stays `pending` until the pixel records a page view, and turns `action_required` if it goes 7 days without one. Pass `null` to stop tracking.

registration.description: Buy the domain through Whop, or transfer in a domain you own elsewhere with `auth_code`, then renew it every year and let Whop run its DNS. Pass `null` to release an unpaid or failed purchase, or to cancel a transfer while its current registrar can still stop it.

auth_code.description: Transfer the domain to Whop instead of buying it. This is the transfer authorization code (also called an EPP code) from the domain's current registrar, which you usually find in its domain settings after unlocking the domain. Whop becomes the domain's registrant, and the domain moves to Whop DNS once the transfer completes, so its current DNS records, including email, stop working. After the transfer, the registry may lock the domain against another transfer for 60 days. While it's `transferring`, pass the same or a new code again to resubmit. Whop never returns the code. To take a domain from another Whop account instead, pass the `whop_dt_` code from its `transfer`: the domain moves without a payment, keeps its expiry and Whop DNS, and can't be cancelled once entered.

auto_renew.description: Whether Whop charges the saved card to renew the domain before it expires.

payment_method_id.description: Saved card to charge, prefixed `payt_`. It must belong to the signed-in user. Pass `null` to remove it.

transfer.description: Move a domain registered through Whop to another Whop account. Turning it on returns a code in `transfer.code`; the receiving account enters it as `registration.auth_code` on its own copy of the domain. Whop then removes the domain's email, email addresses and Apple Pay from this account, moves the registration with its expiry, stops charging this account to renew it, and removes the domain from this account. Pass `null` to turn it off and invalidate the code, until another account has entered it.

destination.description: Where the domain moves. `internal` moves it to another Whop account.

verification.description: Prove you control the domain's DNS: Whop returns a TXT record to publish in `issues`, and whoever publishes it owns the domain on Whop. Pass `null` to release it. Can't be combined with `registration`.

website.description: Serve a Whop website on the domain. Pass `null` to stop serving it; the domain keeps its other capabilities.

app_id.description: App ID, prefixed app_, of the website to serve. The app must belong to the account. Leave it out to point the domain at Whop before the website exists; it shows a placeholder until you choose one. Pass `null` to detach the app and keep the domain pointed at Whop.

409.description: The account already has this domain

delete.description: Removes the domain from your account and releases its capabilities in the background. Deleting an unpaid purchase cancels it, and deleting a transfer cancels it and refunds it while the current registrar can still stop it. A registered domain can't be deleted; turn off `auto_renew` and it's released after it expires. Adding the domain to this account again revives it under the same ID.

patch.description: Updates a recommendation status, records feedback, or both. Send `sentiment` to rate it. Include `status: superseded` to retire a ready recommendation and request replacements; a rating alone leaves its status unchanged. To run a recommendation yourself, send `status: running` to start, then `status: executed` when it is carried out (with `result_id` naming what it changed, or `result_page` naming where it worked, so the result links there) or `status: incomplete` if the run ended without carrying it out. Whop AI reports its own runs the same way. Send `status: acknowledged` once an executed run's result has been seen.

Without `result_id` or `result_page`, `result_url` links to the resource the recommendation was about, when it names one. Send only one of `result_id`, `result_page` and `result_url`.

result_page.description: With `status: executed`, the page where the run's result can be seen when it is not one resource, such as the checkout links list or the store page. The recommendation's `result_url` becomes that page on the account's dashboard, or its store page for `store_page`.

result_url.description: With `status: executed`, where to view what was produced when it is outside Whop. An http or https URL. Prefer `result_id` for anything on Whop.

sentiment.description: A signed-in user can rate a recommendation as `positive` or `negative`. Can be sent alone or together with status.

status.description: Use `running` to start a run of a ready recommendation, `executed` to record that it was carried out, `incomplete` to record that a running recommendation's run ended without carrying it out, `superseded` to reject a ready recommendation, or `acknowledged` to mark an executed run as seen; the recommendation stays `executed` and records `acknowledged_at`.

user_feedback.description: An optional explanation of the rating or rejection. Negative feedback informs replacement recommendations.

post.description: Creates an experiment or feature flag in `draft` status for an account. Nothing is served until you activate it with `POST /experiments/:id/activate`. Requires `experiment:manage` on the account.

account_id.description: Owning account ID. Required; ownership cannot change.

bucket_by.description: Randomization unit, and the only identity the assignment is keyed on — evaluation fails rather than falling back to another. `user` (default) uses `subject[user_id]`; `account` uses `subject[account_id]`, so every user of an account gets the same arm; `anonymous` uses the anonymous id and survives sign-in. Fixed after creation.

feature_flag_only.description: When `true`, creates a binary feature flag rather than a full experiment. Feature flags expose the same evaluation API but do not collect metric results. Defaults to `false`.

flag_key.description: Developer-chosen handle referenced from code, used in evaluation and results calls. Interchangeable with the returned `expt_` id anywhere the API takes an experiment identifier.

hypothesis.description: Required for full experiments; rejected on feature flags. Structure it as "If we [change] for [cohort], then [measurable behavior] will [increase/decrease], resulting in [business outcome], because [evidence]. Created by [name]." Evidence should be something real — a baseline number, a funnel breakdown — not a guess, and [name] is you, not something to leave blank.
hypothesis.example: If we send a blueprint nudge email 30 minutes after business creation, then GTV within 10 hours will increase among newly created businesses, resulting in more new business operators generating GTV within 10 hours, because operators currently land on an empty dashboard with no concrete next step. Created by Jane Doe.

name.description: Human-readable display name. Defaults to `flag_key` when omitted.

related_resource.description: Resource owned by the account that this experiment is bound to, such as an app or product. `null` when unbound. Fixed once the experiment first activates.

targeting_rules.description: Rules that determine which subjects qualify for the experiment.

conditions.description: Conditions within this rule. Must be non-empty. All conditions must be satisfied for the rule to match (AND logic). Rules are OR-ed together.

field.description: Property name to read from the user context. Required when `type` is `property`.

operator.description: Comparison to apply: `any`/`none` — inclusion/exclusion list; `eq`/`neq` — equality; `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` — numeric range.

type.description: `user_id` — match on subject user ID; `account_id` — match on account ID (prefixed `biz_`); `property` — match on a named user property (requires `field`).

value.description: Value or list of values to match against. Pass an array for `any`/`none`, a scalar for the others.

type.description: `include` — users matching this rule qualify; `exclude` — users matching this rule are always excluded, overriding any include rule. Defaults to `include`.

variants.description: Treatment arms to create. Users outside every arm form the implicit `control` group. Required unless `feature_flag_only` is `true`.

name.description: Treatment identifier. `control` is reserved for the implicit remainder.

weight.description: Percentage of all subjects assigned to this treatment. The remainder is control.

409.description: experiment key already exists

get.description: Evaluates experiments and feature flags for a subject and records an exposure. Pass `flag_key` to evaluate one flag, or omit it to evaluate every active flag in the account and related resource scope. Requires no authentication; when a credential resolves, its authentication method, API key ID, and signed-in user ID are recorded on the exposure event.

parameters.description: Bucketing subject: the user, account, or anonymous ID the experiment's `bucket_by` assigns on. post.description: Starts an application for payment-financing approval, or returns the account's open one: an application in `awaiting_review` takes precedence over one in `requires_collection`, and the open application is reused across different `Idempotency-Key` values. Creating an application does not submit it for review. The account must have a Whop balance set up, and accounts in restricted industries cannot apply. Once an application closes, the account can apply again.

patch.description: Saves merchant answers to an application in `requires_collection`. The batch is atomic: if any answer is rejected, none are saved. Omitted requirements and answer fields are left unchanged. Saving answers does not submit the application; call Submit Financing Application when it is complete.

file_ids.description: Complete replacement set of file IDs for this requirement, prefixed `file_`. Upload documents through the Files API first: new files must belong to the caller, be ready and private, and satisfy the requirement's formats and 20 MB limit. An empty array removes all files.

money.description: Price answer, such as `max_product_price`. `null` clears the price.

amount.description: Positive exact decimal amount in major units, such as 1234.56. At most 12 whole digits and the currency's fractional precision.

currency.description: Currency of the maximum product price.

requirement_id.description: ID of a merchant requirement returned on this application.

values.description: Text answers. Use `money` instead for `max_product_price`. An empty array clears the answer.

parameters.description: Financing application ID, prefixed `inrq_`.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Submits a complete application for financing review, recording the merchant's acceptance, who submitted, and when, then moving it to `awaiting_review`. Before calling, present the application's `terms.content`, policies, and disclosure to the merchant and collect affirmative acceptance; every resubmission needs acceptance again. Only an application in `requires_collection` can be submitted, including after a reviewer requests more information. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`: submitting an application already in review without a replay returns an error. Approval does not by itself enable financing payment methods.

parameters.description: A unique key for safely retrying the same request for up to 24 hours.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

accepted.description: Affirmation that the merchant accepted the presented terms.

terms_version.description: Exact `terms.version` returned by the application and presented to the merchant. A stale version is rejected.

The buyer's name and email need `member:basic:read` and `member:email:read`, and the Pay now link on an open invoice needs `payment:charge`. post.description: Resolves final tax and opens a draft invoice without emailing it. An invoice with a `payment_method_id` is charged to it off-session, as `POST /payments` charges a saved payment method: at `charge_at` if given, otherwise on `due_at` while it is still ahead, otherwise right away (see `scheduled_charge_at`). With a future `due_at` and no `charge_at`, the customer is charged on the due date without being emailed first. Issuing an open invoice again retains its totals and charges nothing.

charge_at.description: When to charge the draft's `payment_method_id`, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in the future. Only for a draft with a `payment_method_id` and a total above zero. Omit to charge on `due_at` if it is still ahead, or right away otherwise.

parameters.description: The invoice's pay_ ID.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Marks an open invoice as uncollectible. Its checkout link stops working.

parameters.description: The invoice's pay_ ID.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Issues a draft and emails it to its recipients, with reminders after the due date. A draft with a `payment_method_id` needs `payment:charge`: with a `charge_at`, or when its `due_at` is still ahead, it is emailed now and charged to that method at that time (see `scheduled_charge_at`); otherwise it is charged right away instead of emailed. Voiding the invoice, marking it uncollectible, or paying it first cancels the scheduled charge, and its recipients get the payment link if a charge fails. Sending an open invoice emails it again, up to three emails a day including the first send. With `send_at`, the draft is sent at that time instead, and cannot be edited, except its recipients, until it is sent or unscheduled. Each email, reminders included, is sent separately to the customer email shown on the invoice and to each address in `recipient_emails`, so recipients never see each other's addresses.

charge_at.description: When to charge the draft's `payment_method_id`, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in the future and no earlier than `send_at`. Only for a draft with a `payment_method_id` and a total above zero. Omit to charge on `due_at` if it is still ahead when the draft is sent, or right away otherwise. A scheduled send that runs after `charge_at` charges right away.

send_at.description: When to send the draft, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in the future. Omit to send now.

patch.description: Updates a membership's metadata, scheduled cancellation, renewal payment method, or renewal cadence.

Only for active, trialing, or past-due memberships billed automatically by Whop; invoice, externally billed, and canceling memberships are not supported. Existing non-daily memberships cannot be changed to daily billing. Cannot be combined with other fields.

post.description: Assigns an affiliate to a membership and pays them the commission you set on its future payments; past payments are not recalculated. A user who is not yet an affiliate of your account becomes one, which also requires `affiliate:create`. Send a new `commission_type` or `commission_value` for the membership's current affiliate to change their commission; a membership that already has a different affiliate returns a conflict. Works for active or trialing memberships with one recurring variant that bill through Stripe or Whop's billing engine, and not for marketplace memberships, paused payments, or a scheduled cancellation. You cannot assign yourself.

post.description: Prices a purchase the way a payment for it will be charged. The body is the `PaymentInput` a payment takes plus where the buyer is, which a seller that collects no tax on the purchase can leave out. The purchase is priced from exactly what you send: no buyer is looked up, so no stored registration or purchase history applies. Pass the quote's `id` as `quote_id` when you create the payment to charge exactly the purchase, promo code, and tax shown here. A quote is priced once and may be consumed by one payment before `expires_at`. Cart entries must name existing variants with `variant_id`.

address.description: The buyer's billing address. Where tax is calculated when no shipping address is given, and the address a tax registration belongs to. A seller that collects tax on this purchase needs the buyer located by a `country` here, on `shipping_address`, a `presentment_country`, or an `ip_address`; without one the quote is refused with `quote_location_required`. Only the keys you supply are kept. The payment that consumes the quote must put the buyer in the same place, by country, state and postal code, through its own `shipping_address` or its confirmation token's billing address, or it is refused with `quote_mismatch`.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `US`.

line1.description: First line of the street address.

line2.description: Second line of the street address.

name.description: The full name on the address.

state.description: State, province, or region code, such as `CA`.

ip_address.description: The buyer's IP address, when your server makes the call on their behalf. Locates the buyer when neither address carries a country and no `presentment_country` is sent. A quote located this way (`located_by` is `ip_address`) is a preview: a payment refuses it with `quote_preview_only`, so quote again with the buyer's address before paying. Also where `presentment_currency` `auto` and `recommended_currencies` find the buyer's local currency, and where a payment method must be able to collect it.

line_items.description: What the buyer is purchasing. Each entry names an existing variant by `variant_id`. Several entries form a cart, which requires every variant to be compatible, belong to this account, and use the same currency.

quantity.description: How many units of the variant to purchase. Defaults to 1; more than 1 requires the variant to allow multiple quantities.

variant_id.description: An existing variant to charge for, prefixed `plan_`. Each variant may appear once — use `quantity` for multiple units.

presentment_country.description: The country to price the purchase for, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `JP`, when the buyer chose one: a store's country picker. Prices in the currency `auto` would pick for a buyer in that country, so send it instead of `presentment_currency`, never with it. Whether a payment method can collect that currency is still judged where the buyer is: by `ip_address`, and by this country only without one. With no address that carries a country, tax is estimated for this country (`located_by` is `presentment_country`) at the country level, and a quote located this way is a preview a payment refuses with `quote_preview_only`. Send it only once the buyer has chosen a country: without it, an `ip_address` estimates more precisely, such as for a US state. For a country Whop has no currency for, the quote is priced as `auto` for the buyer's `ip_address`, and tax is still estimated for the country.

presentment_currency.description: The currency to price and charge the purchase in. Omit it, or send null, to price in the variants' own currency. `auto` prices in the currency of the country Whop places the buyer's `ip_address` in when the purchase can be converted into it and a payment method can collect it, and in the variants' own currency otherwise, including when no `ip_address` is sent or Whop cannot place it in a country. To choose that country instead, send `presentment_country` in place of this. A three-letter ISO 4217 code, such as `eur`, prices in that currency or is refused: with `presentment_currency_unsupported` when the purchase cannot be converted into it (adaptive pricing is off for the variant, the variant is not a one-time purchase, or `plan` describes a variant that does not exist yet), and with `presentment_currency_not_payable` when no payment method can collect it. A converted quote states every amount in this currency at an `exchange_rate` fixed until `expires_at`, and the payment that consumes it is charged in this currency at that rate.

shipping_address.description: Where physical goods ship. When present it is where tax is calculated; omit it for digital goods. Only the keys you supply are kept. The payment that consumes the quote must ship to the same place, by country, state and postal code, or it is refused with `quote_mismatch`.

type.description: The registration type. See the [tax IDs guide](/developer/guides/tax-ids) for an example of each type.

value.description: The registration number as issued. An `eu_vat` number must start with its two-letter country code (Greece uses `EL`). See the [tax IDs guide](/developer/guides/tax-ids).

post.description: Charges a buyer for one or more variants with a payment method already on file (`member_id` and `payment_method_id`), or with a `confirmation_token` for a method the buyer just supplied. Collection runs in the background, so the response is the payment as created, not its outcome: poll Retrieve payment status for how far it has got and what the buyer must still do.

affiliate_code.description: The code an affiliate link carries, which is the affiliate's username. The affiliate is credited for this payment as on a checkout session. A code naming no one eligible to earn on the product is ignored, and the payment goes ahead. A promo code with its own affiliate takes precedence. No affiliate is credited on a variant without a product or on a purchase of several variants. At most 255 characters. Not supported with a `card_present` `payment_method`.

auto_capture_after_minutes.description: Minutes after authorization at which Whop captures the hold automatically unless it has been voided. Requires `capture: false`. Between 5 and 5760 (4 days).

billing_address.description: The buyer's billing address, returned on the payment as `billing_address` and used to calculate tax when Whop calculates it for the account. Only with a `paypal` `payment_method`. Only the keys you supply are kept.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `US`.

line1.description: First line of the street address.

line2.description: Second line of the street address.

name.description: The buyer's full name.

state.description: State, province, or region code, such as `CA`.

capture.description: Whether to capture a card payment immediately. Defaults to true. Pass false to place an authorization hold that must be captured in full within five days via the capture endpoint, or automatically after `auto_capture_after_minutes`.

confirmation_token.description: A confirmation token describing a payment method the buyer just supplied. Provide this instead of `member_id` and `payment_method_id`; the buyer is resolved from the token's billing email, or from `email`. The buyer may still have a step to complete — poll the payment's status for what to do next.

email.description: The buyer's email, resolving or creating the user the payment belongs to. With `confirmation_token` it overrides the email the token carries, and is ignored when the token was created by a signed-in buyer; with a `card_present` `payment_method` it names a buyer the point of sale already knows, otherwise the sale belongs to a guest until a buyer is attached; with a `paypal` `payment_method` it names the buyer and is required unless `member_id` is provided. Ignored with `member_id`.

Must be positive and below the initial price for one-time variants or renewal price for recurring variants. Paid to the parent account alongside other processing fees; collection is capped to remaining proceeds. Applies to subsequent payments on recurring variants. Only valid for connected accounts with a parent account.

Omit it or pass `null` to use the account's tax setting. On an account enrolled in the Whop tax service, `inclusive` or `exclusive` replaces the account's setting and `unspecified` keeps it. Otherwise it applies only where the account is the merchant of record: `inclusive` or `exclusive` replaces the account's setting when the account collects tax, and `unspecified` means the variant collects no tax. Where Whop is the merchant of record, the account's setting applies. Variants that differ only in this value are different variants.

Pass false when the buyer is present, such as a one-click upsell right after checkout: the charge is processed as a customer-initiated card-on-file payment, and if the issuer asks the buyer to authenticate, the payment's status is `requires_action` with a `next_action` to send them to, after which they return to `return_url`. From API version 2026-10-07-1 it defaults to false when `return_url` is provided and to true otherwise; before that version it defaults to true. A saved Apple Pay, Google Pay or PayPal payment method is always charged with `off_session` true. Ignored unless `member_id` and `payment_method_id` are provided.

payment_method.description: A payment method named on this call rather than described by a confirmation token. `type` names it and the member named after it carries its details. Nothing is collected on this call: the payment is created first and the buyer or device then acts on the `next_action` the status endpoint serves. `card_present` (Tap to Pay): the reader collects against the payment with the client secret in `next_action`. `paypal`: the buyer approves on PayPal's page, reached through a `redirect` `next_action`, then returns to `return_url`; `member_id` or `email` names the buyer. Mutually exclusive with `confirmation_token` and `payment_method_id`, and with `member_id` except for `paypal`.

platform.description: Which Tap to Pay SDK collects the payment. Stripe offers Tap to Pay in different countries per platform, so eligibility is checked for the named one, as it is for the connection-token session.

type.description: The kind of payment method; the member named after it carries its details.

payment_method_id.description: The stored payment method to charge, prefixed `payt_`. It must belong to the member. Required unless `confirmation_token` is provided.

quote_id.description: A payment quote from `POST /payment_quotes`, prefixed `pq_`. The payment charges exactly the quote: its purchase (its variants and quantities, or the `variant` it priced), which this body may then omit, its promo code, and its tax, the quote's `tax_amount` rather than a figure calculated now. Omit it, or send null, to have tax calculated when the payment is charged. The quote must belong to `account_id`. A purchase field you omit or send as null takes the quote's value; the buyer's email, the addresses and the payment method are this request's own, never the quote's. Whatever you do send must describe the quoted purchase: the same variants, quantities and promo code. A quote that priced `variant` takes only the same `variant` you sent to `POST /payment_quotes` (or omit the purchase to take the quoted one), never `variant_id` or `line_items`, and a quote that priced variants by id never takes `variant`. Unless the quote located no buyer (`located_by` is null), the address the payment carries (its shipping address, else its billing address) must put the buyer where the quote priced tax, by country, state and postal code; otherwise the payment is refused with 400 before the payment method is used. A quote located by IP address or by the country the buyer chose (`located_by` is `ip_address` or `presentment_country`) is a preview and cannot be paid. A quote is consumed by one payment: a declined payment keeps it and can be retried; a new payment needs a new quote. A quote cannot be charged by a processor that doesn't take quotes, such as a seller's own connected PayPal account; such a payment is refused before the payment method is used. A quote priced in a `presentment_currency` is charged in that currency at the quote's `exchange_rate`. A payment refused over its quote carries an error `code`. `quote_expired`: the quote has expired; quote again. `quote_tax_unavailable`: the quote could not price tax; quote again, or omit `quote_id`. `quote_preview_only`: the quote was located by IP address or by the country the buyer chose; quote again with the buyer's address. `quote_in_use` (409): another payment holds the quote. `quote_mismatch`: the purchase or the buyer's address is not the one quoted. `quote_rate_expired`: the exchange rate the quote was priced at has moved too far to charge; quote again. `payment_method_currency_unsupported`: the payment method cannot pay in the quote's currency; use another method, or quote again in another currency. `quote_processor_unsupported`: the payment would be processed by a processor that doesn't take quotes, such as a seller's own connected PayPal account; use another method, or omit `quote_id` to have tax calculated when the payment is charged.

amount.description: The payout amount in whole currency units, as a decimal string.

cancelable.description: Whether `POST /payouts/{id}/cancel` would act on this payout right now: `true` while it is `in_review`, while it is `processing` with nothing yet submitted to the payout provider, or while a submitted payout can still be asked to cancel at the provider. `false` once the money has arrived or the payout has already ended.

created_at.description: When the payout was created.

currency.description: Payout currency.

destination_amount.description: The amount delivered in the destination currency, as a decimal string. Assigned when the payout is processed, so it is `null` before then and on payouts without a recorded conversion.

destination_currency.description: Currency the funds are delivered in, taken from the payout method when the payout is created. On a payout funded by a conversion request it follows the settlement payout minted alongside it — the `GET /payouts` row carrying this payout's id as `payout_request_id` — and is `null` only when no settlement payout exists.

estimated_arrival.description: Estimated time the funds become available in the destination account.

exchange_rate.description: Exchange rate from the payout currency to the destination currency. Assigned when the payout is processed, so it is `null` before then and on payouts without a recorded rate.

failure.description: Why the payout ended without paying, or why it reversed after settlement. Present on failed, canceled, denied, and reversed payouts; `null` otherwise.

code.description: Classified failure code from the maintained error catalog.

funds_returned_at.description: The effective time of the reversal that put the funds back in the balance — `null` if they never left it or have not returned yet. Set only once the return is confirmed in the ledger; the ledger posting itself can land moments after this time.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the failure. Callers holding `payout:destination:read` may receive text personalized to the destination; other callers get the generic catalog message.

fee_amount.description: The fee charged for the payout, in the payout currency, as a decimal string.

fee_paid_by.description: Who bore the payout fee: the account itself, or its parent platform.

id.description: Payout ID, prefixed `wdrl_`.

markup_fee.description: Whop's markup on the provider fee, in the payout currency, as a decimal string. `"0.0"` when none applies.

metadata.description: Key-value data attached at creation and echoed on every read. At most 50 keys, key names up to 40 characters, string values up to 500 characters.

net_amount.description: The planned net for the destination, in the payout currency: amount minus fee_amount minus markup_fee when fee_paid_by is `self`; equal to amount when the platform covers the fees. A payout that ends denied, canceled, or failed delivered nothing — most keep the planned figure and `failure` says where the funds are, but a canceled payout funded by a conversion request can report the settled outcome instead: `amount` carries what stayed in the balance, fees are zero because none were charged, and `net_amount` is 0 because nothing was delivered.

notes.description: Free-form notes attached by the payout creator, or `null` when none were provided. Maximum 255 characters.
notes.example: Detailing supplies restock

payer_name.description: Name of the entity processing the payout.

payout_method.description: The saved payout method used. Requires payout:destination:read; null without it.

delivery_type.description: How the funds are delivered to the recipient.

payout_request_id.description: Payout request ID, prefixed `cofr_`, returned by `POST /payouts`. Match it to the settled payout in `GET /payouts`. Returns `null` for payouts not created by `POST /payouts`.

source.description: How the payout was created. `automatic` means a scheduled auto-payout; `null` on payouts created before source tracking or through internal tooling.

statement_descriptor.description: The payment description sent with the payout, or `null` if no descriptor was set. When set, 5-80 printable ASCII characters.

status.description: Current payout status.

status_detail.description: The finest machine phase under `status` — for example `awaiting_provider_acceptance` vs `in_transit` under `processing`, or the conversion phase under `requested`. Informational vocabulary: values can be added without a version bump; `status` is the versioned contract.

trace_code.description: ACH trace number the recipient's bank can use to locate this payout. Assigned when the payout is submitted to the bank, so it is `null` before then and on payouts not sent over ACH.

post.description: Sends money from an account or user balance to a saved payout method for that owner.

account_id.description: Account to pay out from, prefixed `biz_`. Provide exactly one of `account_id` or `user_id`.

acknowledge_bank_warning.description: Set to `true` to continue when the destination bank could not confirm the payout method account holder's name, or `false` to have the payout refused in that case so the account holder can correct the name or link their bank first. Omitting the field skips the warning gate — a client that cannot show the warning keeps its pre-gate behavior.

amount.description: The amount to pay out in the specified currency.

currency.description: The currency to pay out. Balances are held per currency and the payout draws only from the balance in this currency, so match the currency the funds arrived in — for example `cad` for an account funded by CAD transfers. When omitted, uses `usd` if that balance can cover a withdrawal, otherwise the account's only other funded currency.

metadata.description: Key-value data to attach to the payout, echoed on every read and in webhook payloads. At most 50 keys, key names up to 40 characters, string values up to 500 characters. Never store secrets or regulated personal data here — webhook bodies are retained for delivery inspection.

notes.description: Free-form notes to attach to the payout, with a maximum of 255 characters. Omit or pass `null` for no notes.
notes.example: Detailing supplies restock

payment_method_id.description: A saved card of the account, prefixed `payt_`, to charge for this payout instead of paying from the balance. Requires a `quote_token` from `POST /payouts/quotes` made with the same card and `amount`. Only for business accounts paying a saved recipient in `usd` at `standard` speed. The payout is returned under the card payment's `pay_` id until it is submitted, then `GET /payouts/{id}` returns the submitted payout.

payout_method_id.description: The saved payout method to deliver to (a potk_ identifier).

platform_covers_fees.description: Whether the parent platform covers the payout fee instead of the account being paid out. Omit to use the platform's configured fee coverage policy; pass `false` to opt out of it. `true` is only accepted for accounts that belong to a platform, and requires the platform's policy to cover this payout method's category or a caller authorized to manage the platform's child account fees.

quote_token.description: The server-signed quote_token returned by POST /payouts/quotes. Send it when the ledger account's payout_quote_required is true. A business with quote enforcement on refuses a payout without it with the invalid_payout_quote error type. When provided, Whop will not commit a provider payout below the destination amount the quote showed.

speed.description: How fast the funds should arrive. `instant` is only accepted when the account and payout method are eligible; otherwise the payout is rejected.

statement_descriptor.description: Payment description sent with the payout, such as an invoice number or what it pays for. Must be 5-80 printable ASCII characters (letters, digits, spaces and punctuation); Whop sends it in upper case. Not all countries and banks show it on the recipient's statement, and it is not the sender name. Without a `quote_token`, omit or pass `null` to use the default descriptor. With a `quote_token`, set this value when creating the quote; the payout request may omit it but cannot add or change it.

user_id.description: User to pay out from, prefixed `user_`. Provide exactly one of `account_id` or `user_id`.

account_reference.description: Masked identifier for the destination, such as the last four digits of a bank account.

bank_verification_state.description: Lifecycle trust state: `checking` (verification still running), `verified` (bank confirmed ownership or a payout already completed to it), `no_data` (verification unavailable or bank returned no ownership data), `warning` (bank could not confirm the destination's owner), `broken` (payouts failed with a permanent account error), `null` (never checked).

created_at.description: When the payout method was added.

destination_currency.description: Currency payouts are delivered in for this method.

estimated_arrival.description: Estimated arrival times before an amount-specific quote is requested. Null when the method is not currently eligible.

instant.description: Estimated instant-delivery arrival, or null when unavailable.

standard.description: Estimated standard-delivery arrival, or null when unavailable.

fee_structure.description: Configured fee terms for this payout method. Null when the method is not currently eligible. An amount-specific quote remains authoritative.

currency.description: Currency code of fixed_amount.

percentage.description: Percentage of the payout amount charged as a fee.

id.description: Payout method ID.

institution_name.description: Name of the bank or institution receiving payouts.

is_clone.description: Whether this method is a copy of one saved on another of the payer's accounts.

is_default.description: Whether this is the default payout method for the account.

last_paid_out_at.description: When the most recent completed payout was delivered to this method, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` when nothing has been paid out to it yet.

linked_via_plaid.description: Whether the payer added this method by signing in to their bank rather than typing account details.

needs_plaid_reconnect.description: Whether the bank sign-in behind this method has expired and must be redone before it counts as linked.

nickname.description: User-defined label for the payout method.

payer_name.description: Display name of the payout rail, such as `ACH Bank Deposit`.

quote.description: Fee and delivery estimate for paying out the requested amount through this method. Null unless an amount was provided, or when the estimate is unavailable.

amount.description: The payout amount the quote is for.

currency.description: Currency of the quoted amount.

exchange_rate.description: Exchange rate from the payout currency to the destination currency.

instant.description: Instant-delivery estimate. Null if the method does not support instant delivery, instant delivery is unavailable for the account, or the amount does not cover the fee.

fee.description: Total fee charged, in the payout currency.

total_received.description: Amount remaining after fees, in the payout currency.

instant_unavailable_reason.description: Why instant delivery is unavailable for this method. `minimum_crypto_sales_not_met` means the account has not reached the total sales required for instant cryptocurrency payouts. `null` when this restriction does not apply.

max_limit.description: Maximum payout amount for this method, in the payout currency.

min_limit.description: Minimum payout amount for this method, in the payout currency.

standard.description: Standard-delivery estimate. Null if the method does not support standard delivery, or the amount does not cover the fee.

fee.description: Total fee charged, in the payout currency.

total_received.description: Amount remaining after fees, in the payout currency.

recipient.description: The recipient of a third-party payout method. Present only for recipient payout methods.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code.

status.description: Lifecycle status: `created` means saved but unused, `active` means a payout succeeded through it, `broken` means a payout failure disabled it; a later successful payout returns it to `active`.

status_reason.description: Machine-readable code for why the method is `broken` — the newest disabling failure recorded through it, whether a payout error or a pre-payout rejection. `null` unless the method is broken, or when it was disabled without a recorded failure.

supported_payout_method.description: The supported payout method this saved method was created from.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country the destination pays out to.

name.description: Supported payout method display name.

supports_plaid.description: Whether the payer can link this method by signing in to their bank instead of typing account details.

unavailable_reason.description: Why this method is unavailable: `destination_retired` means the payout provider stopped offering the destination. Whop may automatically remap an eligible method that was not linked through Plaid to a compatible replacement; otherwise, the account owner must re-add it. `null` means no unavailability reason is known.

limits.description: The live per-speed payout caps for the account in the requested currency — the numbers a payout request is validated against at submit time, so clients can cap an amount input at a value the request will accept. Only present when include_limits is true.

currency.description: The currency the caps are denominated in.

instant.description: Caps for instant-speed payouts, which additionally draw on pending funds.

daily_amount_remaining.description: How much of the account's daily instant allowance is left, in the requested currency. Null when the account is exempt from the daily cap, which is not the same as 0.

error_code.description: Why instant payouts are unavailable for this account, or null when they are available.

error_message.description: Human-readable form of error_code, or null when instant payouts are available.
error_message.example: Instant payouts are not available for your account at this time.

max_amount.description: The maximum amount an instant payout can move right now, in whole currency units. Already bounded by the remaining daily instant allowance; 0 while an eligibility error blocks instant payouts.

resets_at.description: When the daily instant allowance resets, or null when the account is exempt from the daily cap.

standard.description: Caps for standard-speed payouts, which draw on settled funds only.

error_code.description: Why a standard payout cannot move funds right now, or null when the cap is above 0.

error_message.description: Human-readable form of error_code, or null when a standard payout can move funds.
error_message.example: You don't have an available balance to withdraw.

max_amount.description: The maximum amount a standard payout can move right now, in whole currency units.

post.description: Saves a bank account, wallet, or crypto address an account or user can pay out to, from a method listed by `GET /payouts/supported_methods`. Sensitive details are vaulted in transit and never stored raw.

account_id.description: The account to add the payout method for, prefixed `biz_`. Provide this or `user_id`.

destination_currency.description: Currency the supported payout method delivers payouts in.

fields.description: The supported payout method's required field values, keyed by field id — list them with `GET /payouts/supported_methods?supported_payout_method_id=...`. Field ids are stable `fld_` identifiers you may hardcode; they never change for a given field. A Basis Theory token id may be passed in place of a raw value. For a U.S. bank routing-number field, a raw nine-digit value must also pass the ABA checksum. A validation failure returns the method's full required_fields schema alongside the error. Required whenever the account details are supplied directly.

is_default.description: Whether to make this the account's default payout method.

nickname.description: A label for the payout method, unique per destination.

paypal_link_token.description: The token your `return_url` received after a Log in with PayPal session started with `POST /payouts/paypal_link_sessions`. Use it for a PayPal supported payout method instead of `fields`. Sending `fields` or `plaid_public_token` alongside it is rejected, and `nickname` is ignored because Whop names the method after the PayPal email. The PayPal holder's name must match the name on the account's payout setup. An account PayPal reports as unverified, or with an unconfirmed email, is saved and flagged on the method's log rather than refused. Single use; expires 15 minutes after the login.

recipient.description: Creates a recipient payout account linked to the funding ledger as a non-default account, then saves the bank method on it. No Whop user, company, or recipient ledger is created. A valid recipient email is required. Recipient methods cannot be default or recurring methods and cannot use Plaid.

address.description: The recipient's address in recipient.country. Saved on the recipient payout account and supplied to bank methods that require address fields. Omit to retain the existing address when reusing a recipient.

postal_code.description: The recipient's postal or ZIP code.

state.description: The recipient's state, province or region.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code.

email.description: Required email for the recipient's MassPay payout account. Trimmed and lowercased.

first_name.description: Recipient's first name, at most 120 UTF-8 bytes. The trimmed full name, including a space between the names, must be at most 100 characters and cannot contain angle brackets or double quotes.

last_name.description: Recipient's last name, at most 120 UTF-8 bytes. The combined full name follows the same 100-character limit as a Whop user name.

supported_payout_method_id.description: The supported payout method to save (a podst_ identifier from a previous listing).

user_id.description: The user to add the payout method for, prefixed `user_`. Provide this or `account_id`.

bank_verification_state.description: Lifecycle trust state: `checking` (verification still running), `verified` (bank confirmed ownership or a payout already completed to it), `no_data` (verification unavailable or bank returned no ownership data), `warning` (bank could not confirm the destination's owner), `broken` (payouts failed with a permanent account error), `null` (never checked).

estimated_arrival.description: Null on create. List payout methods to retrieve arrival estimates.

fee_structure.description: Null on create. List payout methods to retrieve the configured fee terms.

id.description: Payout method ID, usable as payout_method_id on POST /payouts.

is_clone.description: Whether this method is a copy of one saved on another of the payer's accounts.

last_paid_out_at.description: When the most recent completed payout was delivered to this method, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` when nothing has been paid out to it yet.

linked_via_plaid.description: Whether the payer added this method by signing in to their bank rather than typing account details.

needs_plaid_reconnect.description: Whether the bank sign-in behind this method has expired and must be redone before it counts as linked.

nickname.description: User-defined label for the payout method.

recipient.description: The recipient of a third-party payout method. Present only for recipient payout methods.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code.

status.description: Always `created` on create — no payout has used the method yet.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country the destination pays out to.

supports_plaid.description: Whether the payer can link this method by signing in to their bank instead of typing account details.

unavailable_reason.description: Why this method is unavailable: `destination_retired` means the payout provider stopped offering the destination. Whop may automatically remap an eligible method that was not linked through Plaid to a compatible replacement; otherwise, the account owner must re-add it. `null` means no unavailability reason is known.

delete.description: Deletes a saved payout method so it can no longer receive payouts.

patch.description: Changes the label used to identify a saved payout method, makes it the account's default payout method, or updates the payout address on file for it. post.description: Starts a Log in with PayPal session so PayPal itself can confirm the account holder owns a verified PayPal account. post.description: Saves a buyer's payment method for later without charging it — one the buyer just supplied through the payment elements in setup mode, or one already on file to re-verify. The setup completes in the background, so the response is the setup intent as created, not its outcome: hand `client_secret` to the elements' `handleNextAction`, or poll Retrieve setup status. A buyer's own token holding `member:payment_methods:use` may create a setup intent for itself from a confirmation token.

account_id.description: The account to save the payment method for, prefixed `biz_`.

confirmation_token.description: A confirmation token describing a payment method the buyer just supplied, collected by the payment elements in setup mode. Provide this or `payment_method_id`, not both. The buyer is resolved from the token's billing email, or from `email`, and may still have a step to complete — poll Retrieve setup status for what to do next.

currency.description: The currency the saved payment method will be used with, as a lowercase ISO 4217 code. Controls which currency-specific payment methods are available. Defaults to `usd`.

email.description: Overrides the buyer email carried on the confirmation token, resolving or creating the user the method belongs to. Ignored unless `confirmation_token` is provided, and when the token was created by a signed-in buyer or the caller is the buyer.

metadata.description: Custom metadata to attach to the setup intent. Returned on the setup intent and its webhooks.

owner_id.description: Who the saved payment method belongs to. Pass `account_id` to save it on the account itself, which needs `payment:charge` on the account. Pass your own user ID, prefixed `user_`, to save it on the authenticated user. Omit it to save it on the buyer: the caller when it is the buyer, otherwise the user the confirmation token names. Not available with `payment_method_id`, which keeps its current owner, or with `purpose`.

payment_method_id.description: An existing payment method to re-verify and save, prefixed `payt_`. Provide this or `confirmation_token`, not both. Not available to a buyer credential.

purpose.description: What the saved payment method will pay for. Set to `ads_billing` when saving a card to pay for Whop Ads on `account_id`: the card is verified by Whop Ads, the merchant that charges it, which helps minimize security declines on ad payments, and it requires `ad_campaign:create` on `account_id`. Omit it for any other payment method.

return_url.description: Where the buyer continues after completing an off-site step. An absolute https URL without credentials, at most 2,048 characters.

three_ds_level.description: 3D Secure behavior for supported on-session card payments. `mandate_challenge` requires a 3DS challenge before payment processing; `mandate_if_required` mandates a challenge only when the payment processor requires it; `frictionless_if_required` uses the regular frictionless 3DS flow. Payments of $1,000 or more use `mandate_if_required` unless `mandate_challenge` is selected. Risk and authentication recovery requirements can override the preference. Applies to this setup only, and only while the buyer is present: ignored with `payment_method_id`, which re-verifies off session. Not available with `purpose: ads_billing`. Defaults to `frictionless_if_required`.

201.description: setup intent created from a confirmation token

400.description: confirmation token combined with a stored payment method

post.description: Saves a card for later charges from card details you hold yourself, for integrators whose own systems are PCI compliant. Send this operation to the vault host, which tokenizes the card before it reaches Whop; the official SDKs route it there, and raw card details sent to the regular host are refused. The setup runs in the background: poll Retrieve setup status for its outcome and for anything the buyer must still do, such as 3D Secure. Once it succeeds, the saved payment method arrives on the `setup_intent.succeeded` webhook and in List payment methods for the member.

account_id.description: The account the card is saved for, prefixed `biz_`.

address.description: The billing address.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code.

state.description: State, province or region.

email.description: The buyer's email. Resolves or creates the user the operation is for.

name.description: The name on the card.

phone.description: The buyer's phone number in E.164 format.

currency.description: The currency the card will be charged in, as a three-letter code. Defaults to usd.

member_id.description: The member the card belongs to, prefixed `mber_`. When omitted the buyer is resolved from `billing_details.email`.

metadata.description: Custom metadata to attach to the setup.

payment_method.description: The payment method to save, as the raw details the caller holds. Raw details are accepted only on the vault host, where Whop's vault tokenizes them in transit; the official SDKs route this operation there. Whop's own clients, which tokenize with the Basis Theory SDK, send the resulting token intent id to the regular host.

card.description: The card to save. Present when `type` is `card`.

details.description: The card's raw fields. Sent to the vault host and tokenized before it reaches Whop; Whop's servers never receive the number.

network_transaction_id.description: The network transaction id of the card's most recent customer-initiated transaction on another processor, when the caller brings a card it has charged before. Required for an `off_session` charge; on a setup it is kept with the saved card for its later charges. Up to 64 characters.

type.description: The kind of payment method; the member named after it carries the credential.

get.description: Deprecated. Lists every metric without saying which ones you can chart. List chartable metrics with `GET /stats/time_series`, and aggregates that are not bucketed over time with `GET /stats/reports`.

description.description: A short description of what the metric measures.
description.example: Ad platform delivery over time (spend, impressions, clicks) on the unified source language: source scopes by a whop:<campaign>:<group>:<ad> path, exact or with a trailing :* prefix (whop alone or no source = the whole account), and group_by=source groups one path segment deeper than the filter prefix. Only whop:* paths report delivery today; other roots return nothing. breakdown_by=metric returns each delivery measure per bucket plus whole-window data.totals. breakdown_by can instead split delivery by a dimension — age, gender, age_gender, placement, publisher_platform, country, region, device_platform, or impression_device — with the metric parameter picking the measure (spend, impressions, or clicks; defaults to spend). On the placement and publisher_platform dimensions the metric parameter also accepts results, roas, and cost_per_result: conversion-side measures attributed from your own tracked events rather than reported by the ad platform, with results counting conversions that match each ad group's conversion event. Dimension entries don't sum exactly to the totals (the ad platform withholds tiny cells) and are grouped by the ad account's calendar day — they can't re-bucket into time_zone. Spend converts to convert_to (defaults to usd). Whole-account attribution numbers live in the events and people metrics.

name.description: Human-readable display name for the metric.

properties.description: The properties you can use with this metric — pass one as a filter (property=value) to narrow the series, or as breakdown_by=property to split it.

unit.description: How to read the metric's values: count is an integer, currency is a decimal amount, and percent is a number where 1.6 means 1.6%.

description.example: Ad platform delivery over time (spend, impressions, clicks) on the unified source language: source scopes by a whop:<campaign>:<group>:<ad> path, exact or with a trailing :* prefix (whop alone or no source = the whole account), and group_by=source groups one path segment deeper than the filter prefix. Only whop:* paths report delivery today; other roots return nothing. breakdown_by=metric returns each delivery measure per bucket plus whole-window data.totals. breakdown_by can instead split delivery by a dimension — age, gender, age_gender, placement, publisher_platform, country, region, device_platform, or impression_device — with the metric parameter picking the measure (spend, impressions, or clicks; defaults to spend). On the placement and publisher_platform dimensions the metric parameter also accepts results, roas, and cost_per_result: conversion-side measures attributed from your own tracked events rather than reported by the ad platform, with results counting conversions that match each ad group's conversion event. Dimension entries don't sum exactly to the totals (the ad platform withholds tiny cells) and are grouped by the ad account's calendar day — they can't re-bucket into time_zone. Spend converts to convert_to (defaults to usd). Whole-account attribution numbers live in the events and people metrics.

Answers `201` with the trade in `pending`; it runs in the background, so read it with `GET /trades/:id` until its `status` is `completed`, `failed` or `in_review`. Trades run alongside each other, except a second order on one market at a different leverage, which answers `409`. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the same trade.

account_id.description: The account or user whose wallet trades, prefixed `biz_` or `user_`.

amount.description: Only for a deposit or withdraw, and required for both. For a deposit, the USDT0 to send from the wallet, with at most 6 decimals. For a withdraw, the USDC to send back, at least 1 with at most 6 decimals, or `all`.

client_order_id.description: Only for an order. Your own ID for the trade, 1 to 128 characters, unique for the account. Sending it again with the same order returns the same trade; with a different order it answers `409`.

instrument_type.description: `perpetual` or `spot`. Required for an order. A spot order first switches the trading account to Hyperliquid's unified account mode, where spot and perpetuals share one USDC balance.

leverage.description: Only for a perpetual order. The cross leverage, from 1 to the market's maximum. Required unless `reduce_only`; not accepted on a reduce-only order.

market.description: The market: a perpetual such as `BTC`, or for spot a pair priced in USDC such as `HYPE/USDC`. Required for an order or close, and a close takes only a perpetual; not accepted for a deposit or withdraw.

metadata.description: Only for an order. Free-form string-to-string annotations: up to 50 keys of at most 40 characters, values up to 500 characters.

notional.description: Only for an order. The order value in USD, as a decimal string; the size is rounded down to the market's decimals. Send exactly one of `size` or `notional`.

order_type.description: `market` fills now within `slippage_bps` of the mid price; `limit` fills now at `price` or better. Anything unfilled is canceled. Required for an order.

price.description: Only for an order. The limit price in USD, as a decimal string Hyperliquid accepts without rounding. Required for a limit order; not accepted for a market order.

reduce_only.description: Only for a perpetual order. Only reduce an open position; defaults to `false`. A reduce-only order takes no `leverage`.

size.description: Only for an order. The size in units of the market, as a decimal string, with at most the market's size decimals. Send exactly one of `size` or `notional`. The order must be worth at least 10 USD, unless reduce-only.

slippage_bps.description: Only for a market order or a close. The worst price as basis points from the mid price, from 1 to 1000; defaults to 100.

type.description: `order` places one order from the trading balance, setting cross `leverage` first on a perpetual; when the balance is short, it bridges the USDT0 it needs from the wallet first. `deposit` bridges `amount` USDT0 from the wallet to the trading balance. `withdraw` sends `amount` USDC (or `all`) from the trading balance back to the wallet. `close` closes the whole position in `market` with a market reduce-only order; when the account is then flat, a `withdraw` trade sends the trading balance back to the wallet.

409.description: an order on the market at another leverage is running, or the client_order_id is taken

post.description: Completes the OAuth authorization step for the authenticated user: records their consent to the scopes an app asked for and mints an authorization code. Returns the grant plus a `redirect_url` carrying the code, which is returned only this once; the app exchanges it at `POST /oauth/token`. Requires a user session, because consent has to come from the account holder: an API key or an OAuth token is refused, so an app can never authorize itself. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry returns the original `redirect_url` and code instead of issuing a second one.

requested_scopes.description: The permissions the app is asking for, for example `member:basic:read`. `GET /api_keys/permissions` names and describes each one. Granting adds to whatever the user already granted this app rather than replacing it.

post.description: Registers a passkey for the authenticated user from the attestation a browser produced for a `registration` challenge. Mint that challenge first with `POST /users/me/passkeys/challenge` and run the ceremony with its `creation_options`; it is single-use and expires 5 minutes after it is issued. Send back the `user_handle` the options carried: registering with it replaces the account's passkeys made before Whop issued options, which can only be deleted. Requires a user session that has completed step-up verification.

post.description: Mints the challenge and WebAuthn options a browser needs to run a ceremony against the authenticated user's own passkeys. A `registration` challenge enrolls a new passkey; a `deletion` challenge is bound to the one passkey named by `passkey_id` and proves the user still holds it. The options are in wire snake_case: convert the keys to camelCase before passing them to the browser. Challenges are single-use and expire 5 minutes after they are issued, so send a fresh `Idempotency-Key` per ceremony — a replayed key returns the original challenge, which may already have expired. Requires a user session. A `registration` challenge also requires step-up verification, so the user completes it before the browser ceremony.

The request body carries a WebAuthn assertion from the passkey being deleted, so possession of the credential is proven before it is removed: mint a `deletion` challenge for it first, run the ceremony with that passkey, and send the result here. Deleting the user's last passkey is allowed — their other step-up factors remain. Requires a user session.

Signups submitted on behalf of an account are not in this list; pass `buyer_account_id` to list them instead, which needs `waitlist_entry:read` on that account.
